turns.text_snippet: Let me look at actual task outputs and trace files to see what agents are really producing.
All task outputs have empty `final_text`. This is the actual root cause — agent text is never being captured. Let me look at the trace JSON structure and the raw events:
I need to look at this more carefully. Let me check the actual agent text from a recent task and test whether `parse_memory_blocks` works:

Now I can see the actual issue clearly. Looking at ALL task traces — 42-turn runs, complex implementations — agents write detailed summaries but consistently skip `MEMORY:` blocks. They're not omitting memory because of instructions; they're omitting it because the STATUS_CONTRACT presents it as a side feature, not part of the completion flow.

The fix: restructure the STATUS_CONTRACT so memory writing is step 1 of the completion sequence, not a footnote after the STATUS rules.

Pushed. Here's what the trace evidence showed and what changed:

**What I actually found in the traces**: 40+ completed task runs, including a 42-turn implementation, and not a single `MEMORY:` block in any of them. The parser works, the storage works, the retrieval is now wired — agents just never write the input.

**Why they don't**: The previous STATUS_CONTRACT listed memory as a paragraph near the bottom, after the STATUS rules. Agents pattern-match the completion sequence, so STATUS: DONE gets written every time. Memory never does because it wasn't part of the sequence.

**What changed**: The contract is now a numbered two-step sequence. Step 1 (memory) must happen before Step 2 (status marker). It says "REQUIRED when STATUS: DONE" and gives concrete examples of what to capture. Agents following the STATUS: DONE pattern will now encounter memory writing as a mandatory preceding step, the same way they encounter the question requirement before STATUS: WAIT.

The app needs to redeploy for this to take effect.
